name: Jay
caption: The diary's first-person narrator, a man who bought the head booker's job at an auction for one dollar and spends the first months trying to find a replacement so he can be fired. On screen he is Jacob Stranton, a manager brought in by the New Talent Initiative, who manages Umaga and leaves a retirement-home pamphlet on every wrestler they beat down. In November 2007 the narrator, told by Sam Strong that he will be paid ten dollars for an A show, gets it for Pilgrimage and learns his cheque has gone to his apartment; he is made to promise Giant Redwood screen time. On screen, as Stranton, he is put into intensive care by Eddie Peak and misses Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 the narrator writes the year-in-the-job entry (he has made $10 and 'stolen' $102.35), jokes about his girlfriend and the dog's house, and in an out-of-character note moves the diary's real-time anniversary and plans for the Winter Epiphany year-end vote. On screen, as Stranton, he supports Umaga and throws Peter Valentine out of his locker room.

tenures.role: head booker (the narrator); on screen, the manager Jacob Stranton

name: Sam Strong
caption: The owner of USPW, who has put his own money into the company, holds the narrator to a contract the narrator says he never signed and sets him goals on the budget, the profit and the roster. In October 2007 he comes out of retirement to challenge Triple D for the World Championship at A Haunting in America, after Divinity beat his daughter and Human Arsenal drops him through his own desk; the Wild Savages beat him down the Thursday before the show, and Devine beats him with the tights. In November 2007 he signs what Danny Jillefski calls a liability waiver for the Pilgrimage tag match with his daughter against Big Cat Brandon and Eddie Peak, loses it, and learns that the paper made USPW Jillefski's and that he is fired; he gives a farewell speech on the Monday of Week 3 until the Masked Man clears the ring and takes him and Muffin away. In late November and December 2007 he returns with Muffin and Umaga to rescue Stranton, offers Jillefski a match for control of USPW at Winter Epiphany against Big Cat Brandon, refuses to sign the contract in the ring until his lawyer has read it, and has Rick Law in his corner.

name: Danny Jillefski
caption: The on-screen authority figure beside Sam Strong, who makes matches for the shows and grants Freddie Datsun his shot at Bruce the Giant. In October 2007 he sets terms that keep Brett Hall and Bulldozer Brandon Smith apart, books Freddie Datsun against a mystery opponent, and runs the Monday of Week 3 as acting general manager while Sam Strong recovers. In November 2007, as the general manager, he books Pilgrimage, has Eddie Peak put Jacob Stranton in intensive care, tricks Sam Strong into signing USPW over to him, refs the World Championship finish in a referee's shirt, and as the company's new owner opens the Monday of Week 3 with Divinity around him. In late November and December 2007 he agrees under the Masked Man's arm to Strong's offer, has Devine thrown out of his office, sets up a hooded Casey Valentine for Devine, wears a referee's shirt to count Devine's pin on Human Arsenal, takes a phone call from Tommy Cornell, and tells a caller named Vibert that 'Operation Justice just got pushed forward'.

name: Seduction
caption: Darryl Devine's girl at ringside, kidnapped and then impersonated by Peter Valentine. In November 2007 she appears tied to a chair in the Masked Man's video, drops Triple D after he chooses to finish his match, takes Human Arsenal and Fumihiro Ota with her, and welcomes The Hotshots into Divinity at Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 she is struck by Devine and keeps Arsenal in Divinity, finds a message in what looks like her shade of lipstick on Devine's mirror, tells Force that Frankie Perez and Mainstream Hernandez killed the pigeon Mr. Squiggles, hears the Masked Man say he plans to 'be karma', and is given a week by Devine to choose a side.

name: Bruce the Giant
caption: The USPW World Champion when the diary opens, a slow, mumbling chokeslammer who loses the title to Freddie Datsun at Stars, Stripes and Slams and then turns on him. In October 2007 he stands up to Triple D on the Thursday of Week 2, is beaten by him when Seduction counts the pin, and picks Giant Tana, who turns out to be Samoan, as his partner at A Haunting in America, where he chokeslams Umaga for the win. In October and November 2007 he beats Chance Fortune and the Sensational Starfish, loses to Human Arsenal when Phlex and Fortune interfere, and beats Phlex at Pilgrimage with a chokeslam, so does not have to go on Phlex's diet. In late November and December 2007 he wins a four-way dark match, loses to Big Cat Brandon's Brandon Bomb Drop and is hospitalised after Brandon's cafeteria attack, and is mocked by The Best Tag Team Like Ever at his bed.

name: Freddie Datsun
caption: The challenger who beats Bruce the Giant for the World Championship at Stars, Stripes and Slams and defends it against William Hayes, Peter Valentine and Umaga. In October 2007 he stands with Muffin against Divinity and the Wild Savages, beats Eddie Peak in a match the narrator rates an A* at A Haunting in America, and wins the three-way for the World Championship number one contendership on the Thursday of Week 3 with the help of a masked man. In October and November 2007 he beats Umaga on the Monday of Week 4 but has the belt taken from him by Triple D, beats Mean Jean Cattley, leads Team Datsun to a draw with Team Devine, and loses to Triple D at Pilgrimage for the World Championship when the Masked Man hits him with the Slick Trick and Danny Jillefski counts the pin. In late November and December 2007 he teams with Umaga to beat Team Seduction, loses to Big Cat Brandon in 15:56 (A), beats Fumihiro Ota, loses to Human Arsenal, draws with him by double disqualification and is booked with Umaga against Team Seduction at Winter Epiphany.

name: Darryl Devine
caption: A lower-midcard wrestler with the Devine Dream Drop who becomes Darryl Daniel Devine, "Triple D", and is hounded by Peter Valentine for no reason he can find. He keeps the World Championship against Muffin at Blaze of Glory in September 2007, forms Divinity with Seduction and others, and beats Muffin down in a cage match. In October 2007 he keeps the World Championship against Frankie Perez, Bruce the Giant, Sam Strong and Davey Wayne with the help of the Hotshots, Seduction and a pulled pair of tights; a masked man appears above the entrance at A Haunting in America and again on the Monday, and Freddie Datsun walks off with his belt. In October and November 2007 he attacks William Hayes in Japan, stays in the ring to finish Umaga rather than rescue the kidnapped Seduction and Muffin from the Masked Man's video, loses Seduction and Team Seduction, beats Wanda Fish and Human Arsenal in singles, costs Team Seduction the tag belts at Pilgrimage and keeps the World Championship against Freddie Datsun there when the Masked Man hits Datsun and Jillefski counts the pin. In late November and December 2007 he hits Seduction, slams a door on Human Arsenal's forearm, pays Maxmillion Productions to unmask the Masked Man, drags Wolf Hawkins to the ring as the Masked Man and sees the real one revealed as Jack Giedroyc, beats Arsenal (26:35), Rick Law, Hawkins and Reaper, accepts Giedroyc's challenge for Winter Epiphany and wrecks Jillefski's office and Big Cat Brandon.

In October and November 2007 he loses a dark match to Steve Flash and leans on the narrator and Sam Strong for screen time, and is told he can be the corpse in a murder mystery. name: Davis Wayne Newton
caption: A wrestler signed to USPW in April 2007 who pairs with Cameron Vessey as The Hotshots and loses to Wanda Fish and Giant Oak and to Bulldozer Brandon Smith and Trent Shaffer in May. In October 2007 he and Cameron Vessey serve Triple D, he loses to Frankie Perez, and he takes Devine to a 25:55 World Championship match on the Monday of Week 3 that he loses. In October and November 2007 he sits in jail with Vessey for the murder of the pigeon Mr. Squiggles and calls Devine for help, is found guilty and given community service, beats Rudy Velasquez and Art Reed, is beaten bloody by Veteran Mentality, joins Divinity at Pilgrimage and wins the tag belts there with Vessey. In late November and December 2007 he and Cameron Vessey sit through community service, beat Pure Evil and Joss Thompson, and are told by Devine to win at Winter Epiphany.

name: Pete The Hillbilly
caption: One of the Hillbillies, listed with Al The Hillbilly in the narrator's April 2007 roster review.

name: Micky Starr
caption: A wrestler present in Sam Strong's office when Demon Anger announces his retirement in April 2007.

portrays.note: The diary's thread places it in the CornellVerse (a reader's reply about "non-Cornellverse peeps", answered by the author) and the name matches the canon figure of the same name; the diary writes its own continuity, so this is a portrayal and never a merge.

name: Art Reed
caption: A technician the narrator signed in June 2007 and has stuck with a rapper gimmick: he hands out his album's CD, beats Bulldozer Brandon Smith for the National number one contendership, loses a National Championship match to William Hayes, splits matches with Fumihiro Ota, who attacks him, and teams with Triple D and Muffin. In October 2007 he helps Rudy Velasquez beat Steve Flash, then beats Flash at A Haunting in America, and is booked into a three-way with Jacob Jett and Wanda Fish for the National Championship at Pilgrimage. In October and November 2007 he beats Wanda Fish with Jacob Jett's help, loses to Phlex and Davey Wayne, beats Giant Oak, loses the three-way at Pilgrimage, is kept in Divinity by Seduction, beats Eddie Peak with the Dread Lock on the Monday of Week 3, and is destroyed by Peak and Big Cat Brandon, after which Devine puts him out.

name: Brett Hall
caption: A generated 17-year-old the narrator calls solid in the ring and fantastic on the mic, used as an opener: he loses to Giant Oak in June 2007 and is squashed by Umaga on the fourth Saturday of June. In October 2007 he teams with Wanda Fish to beat Jacob Jett and Bulldozer Brandon Smith, rides Smith's motorcycle into a wreck and has his own car wrapped around a pillar, loses the Unappreciated Championship street fight at A Haunting in America, and is disqualified against Brendan Idol on the Monday of Week 3. In October and November 2007 he helps Brendan Idol beat down Bulldozer Brandon Smith, twice.

name: Dean McWade
caption: Listed among the upper midcarders in the narrator's second-quarter 2007 roster review, with Dallas McWade; the diary's later posts give The Canadian Crusties the alias The McWades.

name: Dallas McWade
caption: Listed among the upper midcarders in the narrator's second-quarter 2007 roster review, with Dean McWade; the diary's later posts give The Canadian Crusties the alias The McWades.

name: Shane Sneer
caption: Named with Danny Jillefski and Giant Oak as welcoming the crowd to the show on the fourth Family Night of June 2007.

name: Jacob Jett
caption: Darryl Devine's best friend and former tag partner from Canada, who signs with USPW in July 2007 to stand by him against Seduction's campaign, beats Java, Warlord Agony and Demon Spite, loses a National Championship match to William Hayes, then turns on Devine for Seduction's money and loses to him in August 2007. In October 2007 he loses with Bulldozer Brandon Smith to Brett Hall and Wanda Fish and loses to Fish at A Haunting in America, and is booked into a three-way for the National Championship at Pilgrimage. In October and November 2007 he teams with Art Reed to beat Fish and Giant Oak, loses with Reed to Fish and Phlex, loses the National Championship three-way at Pilgrimage, and is unmasked there as the fake Masked Man who celebrates with Triple D and Jillefski. In late November and December 2007 he beats Peter Valentine, loses to Umaga and is thrown over the top rope by Reaper.

name: Human Arsenal
caption: A hard-hitting wrestler with the Ammo Dump whom Seduction sets on Darryl Devine in July 2007: he loses to Devine by disqualification, is pinned by William Hayes in the fatal four-way, and beats Muffin, Freddie Datsun and Duane Fry. In October and November 2007 he beats Steve Flash, Frankie Perez, Bruce the Giant and Peter Valentine, sides with Seduction against Triple D, loses the tag belts with Ota at Pilgrimage, and loses to Devine in a match of over twenty-three minutes on the Monday of Week 3. In late November and December 2007 he is injured by Devine, beats Rudy Velasquez, Freddie Datsun, draws with Datsun and Umaga, loses to Devine in 26:35, is wooed by the Masked Man, quits Divinity and returns.

name: Chance Fortune
caption: Trent Shaffer's partner, kept secret for weeks in the narrator's July 2007 posts and revealed at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3: the two, billed as the dudes, lose to The Dudez!!!1! in two World Tag Team Championship matches, and he loses a singles match to Frankie Perez. In October and November 2007 he says "your mother" to the Dudez, loses to Bruce the Giant, beats Zeus Maxmillion with a low blow, and loses the I Quit Match at Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 he takes a fall against Ota's team, harasses Muffin, is beaten by her and by Rick Law and mocks Bruce in hospital.

name: Big Cat Brandon
caption: Danny Jillefski's bodyguard, brought in on the Monday of Week 3, July 2007: he flattens Bulldozer Brandon Smith, Wanda Fish and Giant Oak, takes part in the fatal four-way for the World Championship number one contendership and squashes Warlord Agony in August 2007. In October 2007 he slams Muffin's leg in a door, beats Rudy Velasquez, and loses to Muffin at A Haunting in America and to Freddie Datsun in a three-way on the Thursday of Week 3. In October and November 2007 he pounces Muffin off the stage, beats T-Rex, guards the door for Jillefski, and with Eddie Peak beats Sam and Alicia Strong at Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 he beats Peter Valentine and Bruce the Giant, wins with Joey Minnesota over Muffin and Datsun, pins Datsun in 15:56 (A), and is booked against Sam Strong for control of USPW at Winter Epiphany.

name: Duane Fry
caption: A new announcer Sam Strong puts in Danny Jillefski's chair in July 2007, whom Jillefski then throws into matches against Human Arsenal and Fumihiro Ota in August 2007 and who loses both within a minute and a half.

name: Archnemesis
caption: A wrestler billed only as Archnemesis, who is beaten in the multi-man dark matches of July and August 2007, each time in a match won by Steve Flash or Mean Jean Cattley. In late November 2007 he and Evil Machine become Joss Thompson's associates and lose to The Hotshots.

name: Casey Valentine
caption: Peter Valentine's 18-year-old nephew, sent to USPW to train with him, whom Peter insists is his newborn son: he beats Dallas McWade in his first match in September 2007, brushes off the dudes' mockery and, as one of The Valentines, beats Trent Shaffer and Chance Fortune by count-out at Blaze of Glory. In October and November 2007 he beats Maxmillion Productions with Peter by disqualification, loses to Fumihiro Ota, and wins the tag belts with Peter at Pilgrimage for a few minutes before losing them. In late November and December 2007 he is hooded and beaten by Devine, tells Peter he is his nephew, punches him and loses to him in 4:43.

name: Akima
caption: A second Samoan who leaps from the crowd at Blaze of Glory in September 2007 to hit Bruce the Giant with a Suicide Headbutt, costing Umaga the match by disqualification, and whom Jacob Stranton introduces as the killer who will take them back to the top. In October 2007 he kicks Umaga in front of Divinity and is made its newest member; in November he beats Giant Oak and Thomas Morgan in squashes and loses to Umaga at Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 he drags the bound Masked Man to the ring with Brandon, loses to Rick Law by disqualification and is knocked out by Reaper.

name: Phlex
caption: A bodybuilding showman, the artist formerly known as Flex, who comes to the ring on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4, September 2007 to sell his "Phlex-it-All" vitamin supplement for $45.95 a bottle, challenges William Hayes to a match, cracks a bottle over Hayes's head and loses to him, then loses to Freddie Datsun in October; the narrator, who says SWF's loss is his gain, lists him as Frederique Antonio Garcia when he signs. In October 2007 he beats Brendan Idol in the dark matches of the Thursday of Week 1 and of A Haunting in America, beats Warlord Agony and Giant Tana, holds a Phlex-it-All press conference at which three reporters accuse him of steroids, and is slammed through the cafeteria salad bar by Bruce the Giant after insulting him. In October and November 2007 he berates the cafeteria as fat, challenges Bruce the Giant to a match with a diet stipulation, courts Wanda Fish with the help of his old tag partner Pexx as the Sensational Starfish, and loses to Bruce at Pilgrimage. In late November and December 2007 he takes Wanda Fish out on twenty dollars, kisses her under mistletoe, beats Giant Oak and Giant Redwood with Romeo Is Bleeding and is booked as her challenger at Winter Epiphany.

name: Brendan Idol
caption: A newcomer signed in September 2007 who practises American Idol auditions on karaoke and a teddy bear in each bathroom sink, loses to Jacob Jett on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4, and challenges Bulldozer Brandon Smith for the Unappreciated Championship on the Monday of Week 1, October, which he loses. In October 2007 he loses to Phlex, sings a pop song to a stage of reporters, and beats Brett Hall by disqualification on the Monday of Week 3 to earn a challenge for the Unappreciated Championship at Pilgrimage. In October and November 2007 he beats Demon Spite, is beaten by Bulldozer Brandon Smith twice, joins Brett Hall in a beating of Smith, and loses the Unappreciated Championship match at Pilgrimage.

name: Joss Thompson
caption: A wrestler the narrator's September 2007 weekend news lists as signed to a USPW contract, and whom his third-quarter roster review ranks among the jobbers; the range shows him in no match. In October and November 2007, with a neck brace, he defends The Hotshots at their trial for the murder of the pigeon Mr. Squiggles, loses, and blackmails them for payment. In late November and December 2007 he takes Archnemesis and Evil Machine as his associates, jumps The Hotshots and loses to Davey Wayne by disqualification.

name: Eddie Peak
caption: The "Hardcore Assassin", a former DAVE Unified Champion whom Danny Jillefski picks as Freddie Datsun's mystery opponent at A Haunting in America in October 2007: a video shows him, bloody, stabbing a photograph of Datsun with a pen and leaving a corridor of unconscious security guards, he throws a reporter through a wall, takes Datsun through brass knuckles, the steel post and the Spanish announce table, and loses a match the narrator rates an A* when the only referee is down and Datsun pins him with a Patriot Press. In October and November 2007 he draws with Muffin in a match of 27:50, puts Jacob Stranton in intensive care and Sam Strong through the mat on Jillefski's orders, wins with Big Cat Brandon at Pilgrimage, and loses to Art Reed with the Dread Lock on the Monday of Week 3 before destroying him.

name: Giant Tana
caption: A blonde, "Fun Lovin'" Samoan who is the brother of Umaga and Akima and speaks normally, whom Bruce the Giant, who has never realised that Tana is Samoan, names as his partner against The Wild Savages at A Haunting in America in October 2007: Bruce hides on the apron until the finish, then chokeslams Umaga; Phlex, who calls him a whale, beats him on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3 and chokes him with the timekeeper's chair until Bruce and Warlord Agony come to the ring.

name: Jennifer Clare
caption: The interviewer USPW signs in October 2007: the narrator's newsbites on the Monday of Week 3 say that Jenny Playmate takes the place of the show's "non-existent interviewer" under that name from that week's All American Wrestling, and that USPW "can't have Playmates" because it is still partly considered family friendly; until then the diary's interviewer is unnamed and speaks only as "IV". In October and November 2007 she interviews Triple D, who calls her names, Veteran Mentality, Freddie Datsun, the Dudez, The Hotshots, Danny Jillefski with Akima and the Strongs. In late November and December 2007 she interviews Muffin, Robert Oxford and Devine.

name: Nathaniel Johnson
caption: A newcomer who loses a three-way dark match to Robert Oxford on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4, October 2007 and whom the narrator's weekend news says is suspended for arriving late to the Family Night ("Great way to kick off your career kid"). The Family Night of Thursday, Week 3, November 2007 repackages him as the Mantis, a masked man with long black hair streaked red and a spiked choker who perches on the top rope, scratches Bulldozer Brandon Smith's motorcycle and steals his belt; the author says he is the randomly generated worker Nathaniel Johnson, and he wins his television debut over The Trademark on the Monday of Week 3, December 2007 with the Preying Mantis.

name: The Sensational Starfish
caption: A would-be super-villain in a starfish costume who tries to rob Phlex, Wanda Fish and Giant Oak at gunpoint of their wallets "to pay the bills" on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, November 2007, and who turns out to be Pexx, Phlex's old SWF tag-team partner (Pecs), hired to stage a rescue that wins Fish for Phlex: he loses to Bruce the Giant on the Monday of Week 2, beats Giant Oak with the Sea Star Twist on the Family Night of Week 2, lures Bruce into Phlex's ambushes and interferes in Phlex's match with Bruce at Pilgrimage until a costumed hero called The Flash chases him off.

name: Jack Giedroyc
caption: The Masked Man of the diary's long mystery, whom the Family Night of Thursday, Week 2, December 2007 unmasks as 'The Wrath of God' Jack Giedroyc after Darryl Devine's guesses (William Hayes, then Wolf Hawkins) are ruled out; the author notes the Masked Man was introduced on 11 July 2007. He tells the crowd on the Monday of Week 3 that he came to USPW to stop Divinity and Devine himself, that he decided on 1 October to do it ("it was His willing"), that he played at being Hayes to drive Devine mad, and that he accepts Devine's challenge for the World Championship at Winter Epiphany; Reaper watches his back, he cuts Devine's microphone, saves Wolf Hawkins on the tron on the Thursday of Week 3, and on the Monday of Week 4 trades blows with Devine until Jillefski's security pulls them apart.

name: Reaper
caption: A tall, white-eyed, black-robed wrestler with long black hair streaked blood red and a scythe, who first walks into the ring on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 2, December 2007 as the Masked Man's 'associate' and 'The Angel of Death' (the author tells a reader he is the former Jay Darkness, repackaged, in a part first meant for Hell's Bouncer). He knocks out Big Cat Brandon, Akima and Jacob Jett, takes Devine by the throat on the Monday of Week 3, loses a dark match to Frankie Perez the same night, beats Bulldozer Brandon Smith in a dark match on the Thursday of Week 3 with Fade To Black, and loses to Devine on the Monday of Week 4 in 9:35.

name: Wolf Hawkins
caption: Tommy Cornell's apprentice (the diary calls him 'The Prodigy'), on a three-appearance talent trade (the author: one appearance left, the contract runs to June; his first was a dark match against Giedroyc, rated A). Maxmillion Productions, hired by Devine, wrongly tell him he is the Masked Man, and on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 2, December 2007 Devine has Big Cat Brandon and Akima drag him bound and gagged to the ring and beats him in public until Reaper and the real Masked Man stop it; he jumps Devine at the door on the Thursday of Week 3 and loses to him in 22:10 (A*), and Giedroyc's tron message saves him from Devine's chair.

name: Rick Law
caption: A former USPW National Champion (the diary's Where Are They Now? column: the second biggest name to come out of USPW, whose feud with Rich Money led to both being signed by the Big Two) and Sam Strong's mentee, who returns on the Monday of Week 1, December 2007 in a police officer's uniform with a night stick and a ticket book (the author: he is not on a talent trade) to drive Jillefski's Big Cat Brandon and Akima off Sam Strong and Muffin, and joins the faces. He beats Akima by disqualification, teams with Muffin to beat The Best Tag Team Like Ever in 12:44, stops Devine from hitting Muffin and is framed by him with his own club on the Monday of Week 3 (disqualified in 17:59, A).
